title: How do climate scientists make predictions?

lines.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English. I'm Phil.
lines.zh: 哈囉，這裡是 BBC Learning English 的《6 Minute English》。我是 Phil。

lines.en: And I'm Pippa.
lines.zh: 我是 Pippa。

lines.en: This summer is becoming one of the hottest ever with heatwaves across Europe.
lines.zh: 今年夏天正成為史上最熱的夏天之一，歐洲各地都出現熱浪。

lines.en: Here in the UK, a new record for the highest June temperature was set at a sweltering 37.7°C.
lines.zh: 在英國這裡，六月最高溫創下新紀錄，高達悶熱的攝氏 37.7 度。

lines.en: It seems that year after year, temperatures are going up.
lines.zh: 氣溫似乎一年比一年高。

lines.en: In 2015, the COP21 summit agreed to limit global warming to 1.5°C, but since then research shows temperatures exceeding that, leading to warnings of catastrophic damage to Earth's life support systems.
lines.zh: 2015 年，COP21 高峰會同意把全球暖化限制在攝氏 1.5 度以內，但之後的研究顯示氣溫已經超過這個數字，於是有人警告地球的維生系統會遭受災難性的破壞。

lines.en: In this episode, we'll be discussing how hot the planet could get, using some useful new vocabulary.
lines.zh: 在這一集，我們會用一些實用的新詞彙，討論地球可能會變得多熱。

lines.en: And remember, you'll find a free transcript to read along with on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
lines.zh: 別忘了，我們的網站 bbclearningenglish.com 上有免費的逐字稿，可以邊聽邊看。

lines.en: But first, I have a question for you, Phil.
lines.zh: 不過首先，Phil，我有個問題要問你。

lines.en: Scientists monitor climate change using the Earth's energy imbalance – the difference between the solar energy entering the Earth's atmosphere and the radiation going back out into space.
lines.zh: 科學家用「地球能量失衡」來監測氣候變遷——也就是進入地球大氣層的太陽能量，和輻射回太空的能量之間的差距。

lines.en: But which unit do scientists use for this?
lines.zh: 那麼，科學家用哪一種單位來衡量它？

lines.en: Is it: a) Fahrenheit, b) Watts per square metre, or c) Joules?
lines.zh: 是：a) 華氏度、b) 每平方公尺瓦特數，還是 c) 焦耳？

lines.en: Ooh, I know Joules is something to do with energy, so I'm going to go with c).
lines.zh: 喔，我知道焦耳跟能量有關，所以我選 c)。

lines.en: Well, we'll find out the answer at the end of the programme, although careful listeners might hear the answer sooner.
lines.zh: 我們會在節目最後揭曉答案，不過仔細聽的人可能會提早聽到答案。

lines.en: Ooh!
lines.zh: 喔！

lines.en: Yes, exciting!
lines.zh: 對，很刺激吧！

lines.en: So, how do scientists calculate the effects of climate change in the first place?
lines.zh: 那麼，科學家一開始是怎麼計算氣候變遷的影響的？

lines.en: The answer is with models.
lines.zh: 答案是用模型。

lines.en: Huge amounts of physical and chemical data are fed into supercomputers, which then paint pictures of possible futures on Earth.
lines.zh: 大量的物理和化學數據被輸入超級電腦，超級電腦再描繪出地球可能的未來樣貌。

lines.en: But, as NASA climate scientist Kate Marvel explained to BBC World Service programme The Climate Question, nothing is certain.
lines.zh: 但正如 NASA 氣候科學家 Kate Marvel 向 BBC 世界廣播節目《The Climate Question》所解釋的，沒有什麼是確定的。

lines.en: Climate models don't make predictions – they make projections.
lines.zh: 氣候模型不做預測（prediction）——它們做的是推估（projection）。

lines.en: Predictions are saying this is what will happen and a projection is conditional.
lines.zh: 預測是說「這件事會發生」，而推估是有條件的。

lines.en: A projection is: If we do this, then this will happen.
lines.zh: 推估是：如果我們這樣做，就會發生這樣的事。

lines.en: Climate models don't make predictions.
lines.zh: 氣候模型不做預測。

lines.en: Those are statements about what's likely to happen.
lines.zh: 預測是關於可能會發生什麼事的陳述。

lines.en: Instead, they make projections about different possible futures, and these depend on many things.
lines.zh: 相反地，它們針對各種可能的未來做出推估，而這些推估取決於很多因素。

lines.en: In other words, climate models are conditional, meaning that they depend on other factors.
lines.zh: 換句話說，氣候模型是有條件的，意思是它們取決於其他因素。

lines.en: The main factor in climate change, of course, is human activity, especially greenhouse gas emissions.
lines.zh: 當然，氣候變遷的主要因素是人類活動，特別是溫室氣體排放。

lines.en: Another influence on climate models is clouds.
lines.zh: 另一個影響氣候模型的是雲。

lines.en: We usually associate hot summers with cloudless blue skies, but in fact clouds play a big part in the climate, as Kate Marvel explained to the BBC World Service.
lines.zh: 我們通常會把炎熱的夏天和萬里無雲的藍天聯想在一起，但其實雲在氣候中扮演很重要的角色，正如 Kate Marvel 向 BBC 世界廣播解釋的。

lines.en: So, the thing about clouds is that they have this dual effect.
lines.zh: 雲的重點在於它們有雙重作用。

lines.en: They both cool the planet by blocking sunlight, and they warm the planet because they have their own greenhouse effect.
lines.zh: 它們一方面會遮擋陽光讓地球降溫，另一方面又會讓地球變暖，因為它們本身有溫室效應。

lines.en: Right now, the unit that scientists use to measure the energy imbalance of the planet – how much it's out of whack – is Watts, like in a light bulb, per square metre.
lines.zh: 目前，科學家用來衡量地球能量失衡——也就是地球失衡到什麼程度——的單位，是每平方公尺的瓦特數，就是燈泡用的那個瓦特。

lines.en: Kate starts by saying, The thing about clouds is.
lines.zh: Kate 一開始說：The thing about clouds is（雲的重點在於）。

lines.en: She uses the expression 'the thing about' to introduce the most important detail about something.
lines.zh: 她用「the thing about」這個說法，來帶出某件事最重要的細節。

lines.en: Here, that detail is that clouds both cool the planet by blocking sunlight, but also warm it by trapping heat.
lines.zh: 在這裡，那個細節就是：雲一方面遮擋陽光讓地球降溫，另一方面也會困住熱讓地球變暖。

lines.en: So, climate models monitor clouds to accurately measure how much the Earth is out of whack.
lines.zh: 所以氣候模型會監測雲，才能準確衡量地球失衡的程度。

lines.en: If something is out of whack, it's out of balance and not working properly.
lines.zh: 如果某樣東西「out of whack」，就是它失去平衡、運作不正常。

lines.en: Hmm. Climate models sound very complicated to me, Pippa.
lines.zh: 嗯。Pippa，我覺得氣候模型聽起來非常複雜。

lines.en: For one thing, how can you monitor clouds which are constantly moving and changing?
lines.zh: 首先，要怎麼監測不斷移動和變化的雲呢？

lines.en: Yeah. And how much information from around the world would the supercomputers need to make accurate projections?
lines.zh: 對啊。而且超級電腦需要多少來自世界各地的資訊，才能做出準確的推估？

lines.en: It's a concern that BBC presenter Graihagh Jackson raised with Kate Marvel for BBC World Service programme The Climate Question.
lines.zh: 這是 BBC 主持人 Graihagh Jackson 在 BBC 世界廣播節目《The Climate Question》中向 Kate Marvel 提出的疑慮。

lines.en: Surely we need to know the trajectory we're heading in, in order to adapt.
lines.zh: 我們當然需要知道自己正朝哪個方向走，才能去調適吧。

lines.en: Oh absolutely.
lines.zh: 喔，絕對是。

lines.en: You know, I am very pro-science.
lines.zh: 你知道，我非常支持科學。

lines.en: I am very pro-doing science because no climate change is unfortunately not on the table.
lines.zh: 我非常支持做科學研究，因為很遺憾，「完全沒有氣候變遷」已經不是選項了。

lines.en: Kate is very pro-science.
lines.zh: Kate 非常支持科學。

lines.en: If you're pro-something, it means you're in favour of it.
lines.zh: 如果你是 pro-某件事，意思是你贊成它。

lines.en: Models are complex, but they're necessary because unfortunately no climate change at all is not on the table, and that's an idiom, meaning it's not an option.
lines.zh: 模型很複雜，但它們是必要的，因為很遺憾，「完全沒有氣候變遷」已經 not on the table，這是一個慣用語，意思是它不是一個選項。

lines.en: If all this sounds a bit depressing.
lines.zh: 如果這些聽起來有點令人沮喪的話——

lines.en: Kate's final message is more hopeful.
lines.zh: Kate 最後的訊息比較有希望。

lines.en: Climate models prove beyond doubt that the problem of global warming is created by humans, so we know beyond doubt that the solution is also in our hands.
lines.zh: 氣候模型毫無疑問地證明全球暖化的問題是人類造成的，所以我們也確定，解決方法同樣掌握在我們手中。

lines.en: Now, Pippa, careful listeners might already know, but go ahead and reveal the correct answer to your question.
lines.zh: 好了，Pippa，仔細聽的人可能已經知道了，不過還是請你揭曉問題的正確答案。

lines.en: Yes. I asked you, Which unit do scientists use to measure the Earth's energy imbalance?
lines.zh: 好。我問你：科學家用哪一種單位來衡量地球的能量失衡？

lines.en: And the answer was Watts per square metre.
lines.zh: 答案是每平方公尺瓦特數。

lines.en: And I didn't know that, Phil.
lines.zh: 我之前不知道耶，Phil。

lines.en: Right, it's time to recap the vocabulary we heard during this programme.
lines.zh: 好，現在來複習這集節目中聽到的詞彙。

lines.en: A prediction is a statement about what you think will happen in the future.
lines.zh: prediction 是你對未來會發生什麼事的陳述。

lines.en: The adjective 'conditional' means depending on other factors.
lines.zh: 形容詞「conditional」的意思是取決於其他因素。

lines.en: You can use the informal expression 'the thing about' to introduce the most important feature or detail of something.
lines.zh: 你可以用非正式的說法「the thing about」來帶出某件事最重要的特點或細節。

lines.en: The phrase 'out of whack' means out of balance and not working properly.
lines.zh: 片語「out of whack」的意思是失去平衡、運作不正常。

lines.en: If you're pro-something, you're in favour of it.
lines.zh: 如果你是 pro-某件事，就表示你贊成它。

lines.en: And if something is not on the table, it's not an option.
lines.zh: 如果某件事 not on the table，就表示它不是一個選項。

lines.en: It's not available to us.
lines.zh: 我們沒有這個選擇。

lines.en: That's the end of this episode of 6 Minute English.
lines.zh: 這一集的《6 Minute English》就到這裡。

lines.en: Find a worksheet and quiz on our website to test what you've learned.
lines.zh: 到我們的網站找學習單和測驗，檢驗你學到了什麼。

lines.en: We'll be back next week with another episode, so make sure you don't miss it.
lines.zh: 我們下週會帶來另一集，千萬別錯過。

lines.en: Bye for now.
lines.zh: 先說再見了。

lines.en: Bye!
lines.zh: 再見！
